By  Oliver Knight | Edited by  Sheldon Reback Oct 20, 2026, 6:22 a.m. EDT 3  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Options traders lean bearish (Deribit data) 要約 表示 Bitcoin slipped to around $81,400, down 0.5% since midnight UTC, even after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs drew $526.6 million on Monday, their largest daily inflow in nearly a month. South Korea’s Kospi fell 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined, with renewed AI spending worries weighing on chipmakers’ shares. Options traders are seeking downside protection, with Deribit puts outtrading calls by more than two to one and a bearish skew across expiries. CoinDesk’s DeFi index fell 1.2%. Bitcoin BTC $81,462.69 slipped to around $81,400 on Tuesday, down 0.5% since midnight UTC, even after U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted $526.6 million on Monday , their largest daily inflow in nearly a month. Asian stocks set the tone, with South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index falling 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined with renewed worries over AI spending weighing on chipmakers’ shares. Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.31%. Altcoin losses were broadly in line with bitcoin. Ether ETH $2,385.82 fell 0.9% to near $2,385 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) lost 0.34%, compared with a 0.33% drop for the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi gave back Monday’s lead, with the sector index (DFX) dropping 1.2%, the weakest of the CoinDesk benchmarks. Brent crude is near $110 a barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply risks in view. Roughly 70 S&P 500 companies report earnings this week, with General Motors before the bell and United Airlines after the close. Derivatives positioning Bitcoin open interest on Coinalyze fell to $27.4 billion, down 0.6% over 24 hours, while the aggregated funding rate was roughly 8.8% annualized. Ether’s funding of about 3.9% annualized suggests a bullish bias among traders. Longs hold around 55% of bitcoin positions , Coinalyze data shows, with a long/short ratio of 1.24. Binance’s top traders show a similar tilt, with a BTC-USDT position ratio of 1.78 on CoinGlass. Puts outtraded calls by more than two to one on Deribit over 24 hours, with the Oct. 30 $80,000 put the busiest contract. Out-of-the-money puts also cost more than equivalent calls, by 2.5 to 4 volatility points across expiries, a bearish skew that shows traders paying for downside protection even as open interest leans toward calls at $90,000-$100,000 for Oct. 30. CoinGlass shows $155.1 million of liquidations over 24 hours, down 54.7% from the previous day, with longs about 69% of the total on CoinMarketCap’s tally. Bitcoin and ether each saw around $30 million on Coinalyze, together about half of the $120.6 million it tracked. Token talk Celestia (TIA) rose 2.2% to around 63 cents, the biggest gainer on the CoinDesk 100 Index (CD100), adding to a gain of about 42% over the month. The run has coincided with Celestia’s Oct. 1 benchmark showing its Fibre scaling system averaging 3.07 terabits per second. At the same time, options exchange Derive chose Celestia for data availability in its V3 release. The next test is an unlock of 5.58 million TIA on Oct. 31, according to Tokenomist. Sandbox SAND $0.05742 led the CD100 lower with a 4.5% drop to about 6 cents, giving back part of a gain of about 30% over the month. That rally began after South Korean crypto exchanges Upbit, Bithumb and Coinone lifted trading cautions imposed in August following a bridge exploit. Layer-2 tokens were among the weakest, with arbitrum ARB $0.1891 falling 3.6% and starknet STRK $0.05656 dropping 3.2%. Starknet remains up about 29% over the month after surging on Oct. 9 and 10, when the network said it was considering becoming a standalone quantum-resistant layer-1 by 2027. DeFi tokens handed back more of Monday’s rally, with uniswap (UNI) losing 2.3% to about $7.14 and morpho MORPHO $2.4161 down 2.5%. UNI has slumped about 20% over the month even though its fee switch lifted protocol revenue to $14.81 million in September, its strongest month since it began retaining fees, according to Token Terminal. Ethena (ENA) fell 1.9%, extending a decline of about 30% over the month from a late-September peak near 29 cents. By  Jesse Hamilton | Edited by  Stephen Alpher Oct 19, 2026, 12:47 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on CME Group hasn't shown it's being hurt by the new U.S. perpetual futures policies, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission contends. (CoinDesk) Summary Show The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking to cast doubt on CME Group's legal challenge to its new perps policy. The CFTC filed a brief in court arguing that the derivatives giant hasn't shown it's being harmed by the government's new push into perpetual futures, and without harm, it doesn't have legal standing. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission threw open the doors for perpetual futures in the U.S. in May, approving the first bitcoin perp from Kalshi and suggesting that it was open for business on ensuring a domestic surge in such contracts. But the CME Group objected in court , and the CFTC has responded in court that the derivatives giant has no right to get in the way. "Allegations of increased competition, without any plausible inference of an imminent financial injury," don't give CME the legal standing to challenge the CFTC's actions, the agency said in a brief filed on Friday, noting that volume in crypto futures at the CME has actually risen since its policy shift. Perp contracts had soared overseas, becoming a major form of transaction in crypto derivatives, and the CFTC's move sought to clarify how the market could get rolling in the U.S. The agency — in response to President Donald Trump's aggressive crypto agenda that included bringing perps into domestic trading — said it'll regulate the products on a case-by-case basis as futures . Perps allow traders to speculate on the future price of an asset with a typically leveraged position, and the contracts don't come with a built-in expiration. But CME, which operates the leading global venues for derivatives trading, has insisted the contracts are not futures, because they have no end date. They're really swaps, the company's argument would have it, which would come with an entirely different regulatory approach. Spokespeople for CME didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the CFTC's latest filing. The CFTC first asked a federal judge to dismiss CME's case last month, and this latest filing details its argument against the company's legal standing. "CME must plausibly allege an actual or imminent increase in competition," the CFTC argued. "CME has not even done that." The agency argued that CME has been telling investors that it hasn't heard of a demand for perps and that they aren't substitutes for the futures it's offering. "CME cannot have it one way with the court and another way with the investing public on earnings calls," the CFTC contended in its brief. Jaret Seiberg, a policy analyst at TD Cowen, argued in a Monday client note that CME may still have the edge, in both its standing as a competitor and its argument that perps may be appropriately treated as swaps. By  Jesse Hamilton | Edited by  Nikhilesh De Oct 19, 2026, 4:21 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino suggests Senator Richard Blumenthal was fair in his probe of Iran transactions. (Helene Braun/CoinDesk) Summary Show Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino posted on X that his company is often way ahead of government sanctions when it freezes suspicious transactions — a point he contends a recent report from Senate Democrats ignored. He said he's confident Tether is "doing the right thing." Tether is answering back against a report issued last month by Democrats on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations that had accused the stablecoin firm of providing "a significant financial lifeline within Iran's shadow banking network," with Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino saying Monday that the probe missed the positive work it's doing to observe sanctions. Senator Richard Blumenthal, the subcommittee's top Democrat, led the effort, which further highlighted Democratic lawmakers' concerns that crypto is used to support illicit finance. But Ardoino contends that Tether freezes suspicious transactions well before entities such as the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control and Israel's National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing formally flag them. "Senator Blumenthal's 'analysis' of Tether's sanctions report misses that, since 2023, Tether froze on average 4 weeks prior to OFAC & NBCTF official sanction designation and for 99% of the times Tether froze the reported addresses before Chainalysis labelled them," Ardoino wrote in a post on social media site X . Ardoino went on to argue that the company's actions "led to Iran-linked stablecoin volumes declining by 94%." Tether's CEO also spoke remotely at a Washington event, DC Fintech Week, and addressed the senator's report there, as well, last Tuesday. He criticized how it was released to the media before his company could review it. "I believe it's important for the public also to hear our side of the story," he said. "Our aim is to push out the bad actors from USDT," Ardoino said. "Those bad actors are moving to other means that are outside of the control of the United States, and now outside of our control." He added that the work "is not finished," but he said he's happy with Tether's role. "I wake up in the morning and I look at myself in the mirror, and I know that we're doing the right thing," he said. The Senate report went back a number of years, focusing in part on the period before 2024 in which it said Tether didn't comprehensively freeze flagged wallets. "This absence of deterrence invited abuse: Terrorist organizations such as Hamas shifted from transacting in bitcoin and a mix of cryptocurrencies to promoting USDT," it said. Since the report, Blumenthal has additionally been probing the relationship between Tether and its U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, which has close ties to the administration of President Donald Trump. Tether also named Bo Hines, Trump's former White House crypto adviser, as the CEO of its U.S. division last fall. By  Jamie Crawley | Edited by  Oliver Knight Oct 20, 2026, 7:10 a.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on (Shutterstock) Summary Show JPMorgan projects bitcoin will return 10% annually over the next decade in its base case, outpacing its forecasts for U.S. stocks, bonds and gold. The bank’s first range of long-term bitcoin forecasts spans from a 9.7% annual loss in its bear case to a 17% annual gain in its bull case. JPMorgan remains cautious about bitcoin, describing it as a speculative asset whose volatility and unstable correlations hinder its widespread inclusion in investment portfolios. Investment banking behemoth JPMorgan (JPM) expects bitcoin BTC $81,462.69 to outperform U.S. stocks, bonds and gold over the next 10 years. JPMorgan forecasted a base case of 10% annualized returns for bitcoin over the next 10 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report on Tuesday. The bank also set a bear case of -9.7% and a bull case of 17%. The figure compared to projected 5.6%-6.6% growth in U.S. bonds, 7.5% and 7.7% in U.S. large and small-cap equities respectively and 5.5% in gold. The report marks the first time JPMorgan has put a range on bitcoin returns in its research. The New York based banking group has a complicated history with cryptocurrency, largely due to the association of CEO Jamie Dimon’s widely publicized views of bitcoin. Dimon famously described the world’s largest crypto as a “fraud” in 2017, a skeptical position he has reiterated with somewhat softer verbiage in recent years. JPMorgan maintained a cautious view of bitcoin in Tuesday’s report, saying its “volatility and unstable correlation to other asset classes…remain an obstacle to [its] widespread inclusion in portfolios.” Furthermore, the bank does not make a case for bitcoin as a portfolio diversifier, instead viewing it as a “speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing,” according to comments by portfolio manager Dr Sheena Shah and head of digital asset strategy Dennis Cristallo. “It lacks a strategic role in portfolios other than as a bet on fiat currency expansion or future asset trading on blockchains,” they added. “BTC mostly trades like a high beta risk asset that tracks global money supply growth, but it is sometimes treated as ‘digital gold.’ Unstable correlations with other assets present a modeling hurdle. By  Jesse Hamilton | Edited by  Stephen Alpher Oct 19, 2026, 12:47 p.m. EDT 2  min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on CME Group hasn't shown it's being hurt by the new U.S. perpetual futures policies, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission contends. (CoinDesk) Summary Show The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking to cast doubt on CME Group's legal challenge to its new perps policy. The CFTC filed a brief in court arguing that the derivatives giant hasn't shown it's being harmed by the government's new push into perpetual futures, and without harm, it doesn't have legal standing. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission threw open the doors for perpetual futures in the U.S. in May, approving the first bitcoin perp from Kalshi and suggesting that it was open for business on ensuring a domestic surge in such contracts. But the CME Group objected in court , and the CFTC has responded in court that the derivatives giant has no right to get in the way. \"Allegations of increased competition, without any plausible inference of an imminent financial injury,\" don't give CME the legal standing to challenge the CFTC's actions, the agency said in a brief filed on Friday, noting that volume in crypto futures at the CME has actually risen since its policy shift. Perp contracts had soared overseas, becoming a major form of transaction in crypto derivatives, and the CFTC's move sought to clarify how the market could get rolling in the U.S. The agency — in response to President Donald Trump's aggressive crypto agenda that included bringing perps into domestic trading — said it'll regulate the products on a case-by-case basis as futures . Perps allow traders to speculate on the future price of an asset with a typically leveraged position, and the contracts don't come with a built-in expiration. But CME, which operates the leading global venues for derivatives trading, has insisted the contracts are not futures, because they have no end date. They're really swaps, the company's argument would have it, which would come with an entirely different regulatory approach. Spokespeople for CME didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the CFTC's latest filing. The CFTC first asked a federal judge to dismiss CME's case last month, and this latest filing details its argument against the company's legal standing. \"CME must plausibly allege an actual or imminent increase in competition,\" the CFTC argued. \"CME has not even done that.\" The agency argued that CME has been telling investors that it hasn't heard of a demand for perps and that they aren't substitutes for the futures it's offering. \"CME cannot have it one way with the court and another way with the investing public on earnings calls,\" the CFTC contended in its brief. Jaret Seiberg, a policy analyst at TD Cowen, argued in a Monday client note that CME may still have the edge, in both its standing as a competitor and its argument that perps may be appropriately treated as swaps. However, the clock is ticking on the new market. Newsletters State of Crypto Examining the intersection of cryptocurrency and government. He said he's confident Tether is \"doing the right thing.\" Tether is answering back against a report issued last month by Democrats on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations that had accused the stablecoin firm of providing \"a significant financial lifeline within Iran's shadow banking network,\" with Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino saying Monday that the probe missed the positive work it's doing to observe sanctions. Senator Richard Blumenthal, the subcommittee's top Democrat, led the effort, which further highlighted Democratic lawmakers' concerns that crypto is used to support illicit finance. But Ardoino contends that Tether freezes suspicious transactions well before entities such as the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control and Israel's National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing formally flag them. \"Senator Blumenthal's 'analysis' of Tether's sanctions report misses that, since 2023, Tether froze on average 4 weeks prior to OFAC & NBCTF official sanction designation and for 99% of the times Tether froze the reported addresses before Chainalysis labelled them,\" Ardoino wrote in a post on social media site X . Ardoino went on to argue that the company's actions \"led to Iran-linked stablecoin volumes declining by 94%.\" Tether's CEO also spoke remotely at a Washington event, DC Fintech Week, and addressed the senator's report there, as well, last Tuesday. He criticized how it was released to the media before his company could review it. \"I believe it's important for the public also to hear our side of the story,\" he said. \"Our aim is to push out the bad actors from USDT,\" Ardoino said. \"Those bad actors are moving to other means that are outside of the control of the United States, and now outside of our control.\" He added that the work \"is not finished,\" but he said he's happy with Tether's role. \"I wake up in the morning and I look at myself in the mirror, and I know that we're doing the right thing,\" he said. The Senate report went back a number of years, focusing in part on the period before 2024 in which it said Tether didn't comprehensively freeze flagged wallets. \"This absence of deterrence invited abuse: Terrorist organizations such as Hamas shifted from transacting in bitcoin and a mix of cryptocurrencies to promoting USDT,\" it said. Since the report, Blumenthal has additionally been probing the relationship between Tether and its U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, which has close ties to the administration of President Donald Trump. The bank’s first range of long-term bitcoin forecasts spans from a 9.7% annual loss in its bear case to a 17% annual gain in its bull case. JPMorgan remains cautious about bitcoin, describing it as a speculative asset whose volatility and unstable correlations hinder its widespread inclusion in investment portfolios. Investment banking behemoth JPMorgan (JPM) expects bitcoin BTC $81,462.69 to outperform U.S. stocks, bonds and gold over the next 10 years. JPMorgan forecasted a base case of 10% annualized returns for bitcoin over the next 10 years in its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report on Tuesday. The bank also set a bear case of -9.7% and a bull case of 17%. The figure compared to projected 5.6%-6.6% growth in U.S. bonds, 7.5% and 7.7% in U.S. large and small-cap equities respectively and 5.5% in gold. The report marks the first time JPMorgan has put a range on bitcoin returns in its research. The New York based banking group has a complicated history with cryptocurrency, largely due to the association of CEO Jamie Dimon’s widely publicized views of bitcoin. Dimon famously described the world’s largest crypto as a “fraud” in 2017, a skeptical position he has reiterated with somewhat softer verbiage in recent years. JPMorgan maintained a cautious view of bitcoin in Tuesday’s report, saying its “volatility and unstable correlation to other asset classes…remain an obstacle to [its] widespread inclusion in portfolios.” Furthermore, the bank does not make a case for bitcoin as a portfolio diversifier, instead viewing it as a “speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing,” according to comments by portfolio manager Dr Sheena Shah and head of digital asset strategy Dennis Cristallo. “It lacks a strategic role in portfolios other than as a bet on fiat currency expansion or future asset trading on blockchains,” they added. “BTC mostly trades like a high beta risk asset that tracks global money supply growth, but it is sometimes treated as ‘digital gold.’ Unstable correlations with other assets present a modeling hurdle. FINMA did not disclose the issuer of the ETF. Switzerland was the first jurisdiction to approve cryptocurrency exchange-traded products (ETPs). Regulation preventing ETFs from holding only a single asset meant such funds could not be defined as such and so were listed under the umbrella “ETP” designation. The weakness carried into U.S. pre-market trading, with CoreWeave (CRWV) down 4%, Cipher Digital CIFR falling 2% and IREN IREN losing 3%. The Invesco QQQ ETF also traded lower, reflecting broader pressure on technology stocks. Bitcoin edged lower over the past 24 hours but held above $81,000, while gold slipped almost 1% to just above $4,110 an ounce. Brent and WTI crude oil each climbed a further 2%. Long-dated U.S. Treasuries appear to be attracting defensive flows, with the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) rising 0.5%.
